title: Parse a key = value settings file
problem: Implement parse_settings(text), which turns the text of a small config file (lines of `key = value`) into a dict, and parse_list(value), which turns a comma-separated value into a clean list. Real config files are messy: blank lines, comments, tabs, values containing '=', empty values and stray commas.
requirements: parse_settings: trim spaces and tabs around keys and values
Skip blank and whitespace-only lines, and lines whose first non-space character is '#'
Split each line at the first '=' only; the rest of the line is the value
Allow empty values; a repeated key keeps the last value
Raise ValueError for a line without '=' or with an empty key; the message must contain the 1-based line number
parse_list: split on commas, trim each item, drop empty items, keep spaces inside items
contract:
parse_settings(text: str) -> dict[str, str]
parse_list(value: str) -> list[str]
expectedBehavior: parse_settings('db_port=5432\ndsn = user=app\ndebug =') -> {'db_port': '5432', 'dsn': 'user=app', 'debug': ''}; parse_list(' a, b,,c ,') -> ['a', 'b', 'c']; parse_list('') -> [].
edgeCases: An empty value, and an empty key
Empty input for both functions ('' split on ',' gives [''], not [])
Items with spaces inside them ('New York')
hints: Conceptual: handle one line at a time: normalise it (strip), decide whether to skip it, validate it, then split it. For parse_list, remember that split(',') keeps empty strings on purpose; you have to drop them yourself.

Specific: strip() with no argument removes spaces, tabs and newlines. A stripped blank line is the empty string, which is falsy. split('=', 1) keeps any later '=' in the value. enumerate(..., start=1) gives you line numbers for the error message.

Implementation: loop over enumerate(text.split('\n'), start=1); strip the line; continue if it's empty or starts with '#'; raise ValueError(f'line {n}: ...') if '=' is missing; split once, strip key and value, raise if the key is empty, store it. parse_list: loop over value.split(','), strip each part, keep it only if it's non-empty.
evaluation: Uses split with maxsplit, not manual index searching
Error messages say which line is wrong and why
